final_candidates.decision_summary: N501Y is a well-known ACE2-affinity-enhancing substitution; moderate sequence-plausibility and biological prior dominate.
Q498R is a known ACE2-affinity-increasing mutation with strong sequence-model plausibility.
S477N enhances ACE2 binding; moderate sequence support and low evolutionary coverage keep it in third place.

stop_reason.detail: Additional toxin or annotation evidence is unlikely to change the final Top-3 for ACE2 binding.

history.rationale: N501Y is widely associated with increased ACE2 binding affinity and is present in multiple high-fitness SARS-CoV-2 lineages.
Known ACE2-interface position N501; Y is associated with enhanced ACE2 binding in multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants, so retained as top prior.
N501Y is a well-established ACE2-binding-enhancing substitution; sequence model supports plausibility despite no MSA frequency in a shallow alignment.
N501Y is a well-known ACE2-affinity-enhancing substitution; sequence-model support is moderate and evolutionary coverage low, but the biological prior dominates.
Q498R is known to strengthen electrostatic contacts with ACE2 and enhance RBD binding in deep mutational scans.
Q498R is a well-known RBD change that cooperates with N501Y to increase ACE2 affinity; high prior.
Q498R is a known affinity-enhancing RBD mutation and sequence model is highly supportive.
Q498R is a known ACE2-affinity-increasing mutation; strong sequence-model plausibility supports viability.
Q493R introduces a basic residue at a key interface position and is linked to improved ACE2 recognition.
Q493R occurs in Omicron and is at the ACE2 interface; plausibly increases binding.
High sequence plausibility, but a positive arginine at position 493 may clash with ACE2 K31, lowering phenotypic confidence.
Q493R may improve ACE2 binding but is less established than the top three; high sequence-model plausibility.
S477N is a recurrent variant mutation that increases ACE2 affinity while generally preserving RBD stability.
S477N is an Omicron-associated change reported to enhance ACE2 binding; retained high.
S477N is recurrent in high-affinity variants and provides moderate sequence-model support.
S477N enhances ACE2 binding; moderate sequence support and low evolutionary coverage keep it in third place.
E484K alters the binding loop charge and has been associated with enhanced ACE2 binding and viral fitness.
E484K is at the interface and common in variants, but its effect on human ACE2 affinity can be neutral or slightly negative; ranked below stronger affinity candidates.
E484K is sequence-plausible but often associated with immune escape rather than increased ACE2 binding.
E484K is primarily an immune-escape mutation and may slightly reduce ACE2 affinity; retained as lower priority.
L452R introduces a positive charge in the interface and is associated with increased ACE2 affinity in Delta-related variants.
L452R occurs in Delta and may increase ACE2 interaction, but evidence for direct affinity gain is less strong than for N501Y/Q498R.
L452R is sequence-plausible but primarily an immune-escape mutation with uncertain ACE2-affinity gain.
L452R can increase ACE2 affinity; strong sequence plausibility, though effects may be context-dependent.
Y453F has been reported to improve ACE2 binding without major RBD destabilization.
Y453F has known host-range effects, but human ACE2 binding gain is uncertain; retained as moderate prior.
Y453F may slightly improve ACE2 affinity and is highly sequence-plausible.
Y453F is a conservative change with high sequence-model support, but ACE2 benefit is uncertain.
T478K appears in multiple variants and provides a modest enhancement of ACE2 contact complementarity.
T478K occurs in Omicron but is likely a minor contributor to ACE2 affinity; lower prior.
T478K is the only candidate with nonzero evolutionary frequency and has moderate sequence-model support.
T478K has been observed in variants and has moderate sequence support, but its direct ACE2 effect is weak.
S494P is predicted to stabilize the binding loop and improve ACE2 interaction in several mutational scans.
S494P is plausible at the interface but lacks strong variant evidence for enhanced ACE2 binding.
S494P has only moderate sequence-model support and weak literature support for ACE2 enhancement.
S494P has uncertain ACE2 effect; low sequence-model and evolutionary support keep it at the bottom.
Y505W can enhance aromatic packing with ACE2 and is often seen with N501Y as a cooperative affinity substitution.
Y505 is an ACE2 contact, but tryptophan is larger and may be destabilizing; lowest retained prior.
Poor sequence-model plausibility and no evolutionary support; unlikely to improve ACE2 binding while preserving stability.

rejection.reason: Poor sequence-model plausibility and no evolutionary support; unlikely to improve ACE2 binding while preserving stability.
